assign.now: measured the shell, then designed all three layouts on paper

log.msg: MEASURED THE ROOM FIRST. No site sidebar takes width at any of the four widths (.sidebar is a drawer, 0px), so .pages is the whole viewport. The page grid's `wide` track measures 3260px at 3440 (x:90), 1751px at 1920, 1178px at 1280 (x:51), 329px at 400. 3260/3440 = 0.948, so `wide` alone clears check (f) >= 0.9 without any box bleeding. Body font is a clamp (14 -> 18px) but `html` declares no font-size, so 1rem is a flat 16px at every width - which is why every wall floor here is written in rem.

IDS. Workbench and Reader are both instances of 3-holy-grail (narrow / wide / narrow) and Catalog is 1-bands with an n-wall inside it. Two of three sharing one id is not a mistake to hide: an id names the DIVISION of the room and nothing else (/layouts/doc/naming/), so a workbench and an article page really are the same layout wearing different content. The practice index says so out loud.

APPROVED SHAPES. Workbench = approved 2 (Docs three-region) with approved 4 (Tile wall) inside its middle track. Reader = approved 2. Catalog = approved 1 (the page grid: gutters, measure, wide takes the leftover, bleed is paint) with approved 4 inside its middle band. None of the three is a sixth approved layout; /imagine/design/layout/approved/ stays closed.

RESPONSIVE MECHANISM: container queries on each layout root (container-type: inline-size), never viewport media queries - a media query lies the moment the page is put in a column or a panel, and this module's own pages may be. The query targets a DESCENDANT grid, because a container cannot restyle itself.

CSS prefix: std-practice-. `std-` is already /layouts/'s reservation in framework/styles/css-scopes.txt line 160, and a census of `std-practice` across every .css and .js under public/ returns zero hits. No new prefix line is needed and no View subclass is declared, so classify() mints nothing.

assign.now: measured, fixed and re-measured: 8/8 checks at four widths on all three, plus the index

log.msg: THE TABLE. Eight checks x four widths x three layouts, read back off the live pages by headless Chromium at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440. Workbench 32/32, Reader 32/32, Catalog 32/32, and the practice index 32/32. Checks: (a) no text or framed box at x:0 - a bled BAND is excluded, because bleed is paint by design; (b) no prose past the measure; (c) no constant where a spacing token exists; (d) a background implies padding and nothing without a background carries block padding; (e) one left axis per STACKED region, plus one axis for every band's content; (f) 3440 uses >= 0.9 of the viewport; (g) the first nav element above the fold; (h) every overflow:auto box named and wanted - there are ZERO on all three pages, the page is the only scroller.

WALL COUNTS, and not one hole at any width. Workbench tiles (24 items, --column 15rem): 1 / 3 / 4 / 8 columns. Catalog cards (12 items, --column 31rem): 1 / 2 / 3 / 6. Catalog footer (6 groups, fixed count): 1 / 3 / 6 / 6. The fold's nine answers (fixed count): 1 / 3 / 3 / 3. The Reader's margin (4 blocks, fixed count): 1 / 1 / 2 / 4. Every count divides its item count at every width - that is the whole technique: pick the COUNT and the COLUMN WIDTH together, and prefer counts with many divisors (24, 12, 6, 4).

WIDTH USED AT 3440. Workbench 3260/3440 = 0.948, Reader 3260 = 0.948, Catalog 3440 = 1.000 (its bands bleed, which is legal because a band is paint), index 3260 = 0.948. Nothing framed and no text touches x:0 at any width.

COLOUR, measured off the composited pixels, not computed from the tokens. quiet ink on the page floor 5.99:1; quiet ink on fill-a04 (tiles, cards, notes, chips) 5.02-5.49:1; --ink on fill-a04 (panel body, tile names, footer links) 7.88-8.62:1; --ink on --prim (the brand mark and the hero's one filled button) 7.75:1; --prim-ink on the floor (the current contents link) 4.64:1. --prim as a WORD is 2.25:1 and is used as a word nowhere on these three pages.

FINDING 1 - the biggest one, and invisible at 1280. The Reader was written with the article track as minmax(0,1fr) and the margin as a clamp. The article paints only --measure (720px at 3440), so the track was 2485px wide holding 720px of text: 1,860px of grey BETWEEN the article and its own notes, at 3440 only. Every numeric check still passed. Fixed by making the middle track the measure itself and the margin minmax(17rem, 1fr), and by laying the margin out as a four-block wall (1 / 1 / 2 / 4 columns) so the leftover is spent rather than left. The lesson is the brief's own sentence: a third region either earns the leftover or it is just where the room ran out.

FINDING 2 - `--gutter-x` re-resolves against the element's own font-size. It is clamp(2em, 4%, 5em), an inherited token, and the Catalog's footer band carried font-size: 0.9em - so its gutter came out 81px against every other band's 90px at 3440. Nine pixels, invisible one band at a time and obvious down the left edge of the page. A band now keeps the page's font size and its CONTENTS shrink instead.

FINDING 3 - `--subtle` is not contrasty enough on a painted box. The lew42 skin's #6a6a6a measures 4.83:1 on the page floor (over AA) but 4.0:1 on the --fill-a04 this module paints its tiles, cards, notes and hero with - under AA for body text, and nobody can see 4.0 from 4.6. This module declares --std-practice-quiet = color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 85%, var(--surface)), measured at 5.97 / 5.46 / 4.97:1 on the three grounds it paints and 9.8:1 on the dark floor.

FINDING 4 - a container query on the box that IS the container never fires, and nothing throws. The practice index declared container-type on itself and queried `practice` for its three columns; it silently stayed at ONE column at every width including 3440. The obvious fix, framework.css's own .grid.three, then gave TWO columns at 3440: its clamp subtracts a flat 1rem for the gap, and --gap is 43.5px up there, so the 1070px track it asked for only fitted twice. Three cards in two columns is a hole. The switch is now written out with the real --gap in it: lower bound calc(100%/3 - var(--gap)*2/3), so auto-fit lands on exactly three, or on one below the threshold. Never two.

FINDING 5 - the theme beats a single-class rule at every heading. lew42 styles headings from `.theme-lew42 :is(h1, .h1)`, a two-class selector in the same @layer theme, so this module's (0,1,0) font-size rules lost on specificity no matter the load order: the Workbench panel's 0.75em uppercase label rendered at the skin's h3 1.5em and the panel's own name at its h2 2.25em. Every heading rule here is (0,2,0) now.

FINDING 6 - found only by LOOKING. The Catalog's top bar is the same markup as the other two layouts' rails, and the container query that turns a rail into a column at 44rem turned the BAR into a column too: 290px of vertical chrome at 3440, shoving the hero most of the way down the fold. All 32 numeric checks passed on that page. Two (0,2,0) rules keep the bar a strip. Same pass: the hero painted its words into the left fifth of a 3260px band and left the other four empty, so at 80rem it becomes a row - words left, the way out right.

FINDING 7 - the instrument found its own defect first. The contrast probe read Chromium's `color(srgb 0.36 0.36 0.36)` - the form a color-mix() result comes back in, channels 0-1 - as an rgb() triple, so every ratio on the page came back roughly DOUBLE (5.99 read as 18.72). Caught because a quiet grey cannot be 18:1. Fixed before any verdict was taken from it. The probe's check (e) was wrong a second time in the same way: it read a deliberate ROW (the Catalog's bar, its wide hero) as a region whose children failed to share a left axis. It now only asks that of regions that stack.

STABLE NAVIGATION, proven rather than claimed. Clicking tile 18 of 24 on the Workbench at 1920: the panel goes markdown -> editor, and the rail's box, the wall's box and the panel's own box are byte-identical before and after (rail [77,48,240], wall [344,237,1084], panel [1455,48,389]). Nothing above or left of the panel moves, because the panel's track is a clamp rather than a function of its content, and every tile carries a transparent 1px border at rest so lighting one up moves nothing.

LINKED, counted on the PARENT. /layouts/ renders exactly 1 anchor with href='/layouts/practice/' ("Three of them built big, at 3440"), so `children:` and the visible md() line are both in. Every one of the six new urls loads with ZERO console errors and zero failed requests: /layouts/practice/, its three layouts, /layouts/practice/doc/ and doc/decisions/. All three folds open and contain 9 answers, 8 check chips, the four-width line and the polish line.

FOR THE BROWSER. Three items, ready for /layouts/browse/items.json once its critic lands - not written by this task, because two agents in one file is the rule nobody breaks. assign.outcome:
**Three big layouts that span 3440 and still hold at 400 — and the polish is measured, not asserted.**

[**/layouts/practice/**](/layouts/practice/) — three picture cards, one line each, one screen.

![The practice index at 1920](/layouts/practice/shots/practice-index-1920.jpg)

- [**Workbench**](/layouts/practice/workbench/) — a rail, a wall of 24 real `framework/ext/` tiles, a panel that answers. `3-holy-grail`; approved shape 2 with 4 inside. Three regions at 3440 and 1920, two at 1280, one column at 400 with the rail as a top strip. **Proven: clicking a tile changes the panel and the rail, the wall and the panel's own box are byte-identical before and after.**
- [**Reader**](/layouts/practice/reader/) — the layout standard's own article at the measure, with the wide screen's leftover spent on a sticky table of contents, four real wire drawings and five real caveats. `3-holy-grail`; approved shape 2.
- [**Catalog**](/layouts/practice/catalog/) — a nav bar, a hero on a `vh` fold budget, a wall of the twelve real layouts, a footer of six groups of real links. `1-bands`; approved shape 1 with 4 inside.

**None of the three is a sixth approved layout** — each is an instance of a shape [the approved five](/imagine/design/layout/approved/) already closed. Two of the three share one id, on purpose: an id names how the room is divided and nothing else.

**Polish, measured.** Eight checks x four widths, read back off the live pages by headless Chromium: **Workbench 32/32, Reader 32/32, Catalog 32/32, index 32/32.** Zero console errors on all six new urls; zero `overflow: auto` boxes on any of them. Every wall's item count and column width were chosen together, so no wall has a hole at any width (24 tiles at 1/3/4/8 columns, 12 cards at 1/2/3/6, 6 footer groups at 1/3/6/6, 9 answers at 1/3/3/3, 4 margin blocks at 1/1/2/4).

**Six things that were wrong and are fixed** — the full record is in [`doc/decisions`](/layouts/practice/doc/decisions/), the numbers in the log below. The two that matter most: the Reader had **1,860px of grey between the article and its own notes at 3440** while every numeric check passed, and the Catalog's top bar silently became a **290px column** at 3440 for the same reason — both were found by LOOKING at the screenshot, not by measuring.

**Left, with the reason.** The three items are not in [`/layouts/browse/`](/layouts/browse/): a critic was editing that module, and two agents in one file is the rule nobody breaks. The `items.json` block and the nine jpegs (named the way browse names its own) are in the log, ready to copy. Nobody has approved these — that is the owner's call by name. Dark-mode ratios are computed from the theme's declared values; every shot is light mode.

log.msg: CORRECTION, and a trap for the next agent: the jsonl  verb is ONLY for a screenshot taken OUTSIDE the repo. Server/plugins/Screenshots.js serves /screenshot?path= from the OS temp root and nowhere else, so five shot lines pointing at public/layouts/practice/shots/*.jpg rendered five grey "no image" swatches and ten 403s in the console. They were removed. A picture that IS a site asset goes in the outcome markdown as a plain url - which is what the landing line does with the practice index shot.

The line above lost its backticks: a double-quoted shell string ate `shot` as a command substitution, exactly as the finish-task skill warns. Said properly: the jsonl `shot` verb is ONLY for a screenshot taken OUTSIDE the repo. `Server/plugins/Screenshots.js` serves `/screenshot?path=` from the OS temp root and refuses everything else, so five `shot` lines pointing at `public/layouts/practice/shots/*.jpg` drew five grey "no image" swatches and ten 403s. They were removed. A picture that IS a site asset belongs in the outcome markdown as a plain url, which is what the landing line does with the practice index shot.

SKILL IMPROVEMENTS, logged here rather than appended to the skills themselves: this task's fence is `public/layouts/practice/**` plus two lines in /layouts/ and this dir, and `.claude/skills/` is outside it — with a sibling agent live in that directory this run (`css/SKILL.md`, `layout/SKILL.md` and `mastermind/SKILL.md` are all modified in git status). Four lines for whoever can file them:

1. **css** — `A CONTAINER QUERY ON THE BOX THAT DECLARES THE CONTAINER NEVER FIRES, and nothing throws.` A box cannot restyle its own container, so `@container` rules whose subject IS the container simply never match: a three-card wall stayed at ONE column at every width including 3440 (2026-09-17). The query must target a DESCENDANT of the container. Same family as the existing `container-type` warning, different failure.
2. **css** — `framework.css's .grid.three hard-codes a 1rem gap allowance` (`clamp(100%/3 - 1rem, …)`), and this site's `--gap` reaches 43.5px at 3440 — so a three-item wall using it lands on TWO tracks up there. Write the switch out with `var(--gap)` in it when the wall must be exactly three.
3. **css** — the theme-trickle warning names `button`; it should name HEADINGS too. lew42 styles them from `.theme-lew42 :is(h1, .h1)` — (0,2,0), same `@layer theme` — so every single-class `font-size` rule on an `h1`/`h2`/`h3` loses on specificity no matter the load order. Two rules in this module rendered at the skin's size until they were prefixed.
4. **layout** — the skill says "widening a column is never the fix for dead space — add a region, or a column, or accept the gutter", which is right but stops one step short of the case that bit here. When a brief also demands the page USE the wide screen, the answer is neither: give the leftover to the region that can SPEND it, and give that region more content. The Reader had 1,860px of grey between the article and its own notes at 3440 with every numeric check passing.
5. **finish-task** — the jsonl `shot` verb only works for a file under the OS temp root (`Server/plugins/Screenshots.js` refuses everything else). A screenshot that is a SITE ASSET goes in the outcome markdown as a plain url instead; five `shot` lines pointing into `public/` drew grey swatches and 403s.
